findings.title: Bootstrap downloads and evaluates remote scripts from mutable, unpinend endpoints without hash validation
findings.attack: T1195.002 supply-chain compromise mutable main branch; T1059.001 PowerShell eval-of-remote
findings.analysis: Origin is the project's own repo (trust implied by choosing to install), but the endpoint is a mutable branch with no commit/tag pin and no hash check: repository takeover, CDN/cache tamper, or an errant merge lands instant code execution on every bootstrapping machine. Same pattern is vendor-recommended for scoop/choco/uv, which raises the bar but does not remove the mutable-origin issue.
findings.remediation: Pin bootstrap to the release tag (e.g. /v1.0.3 path or  redirect through latest GH release asset) and verify the script hash against SHA256SUMS.txt before iex; keep an -Unpinned opt-in for canary testing.

findings.title: GitHub Actions pinned by tag, not commit SHA (incl. third-party action dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable)
findings.attack: Tag retarget on third-party action → arbitrary workflow code → GITHUB_TOKEN exfil (detection_only finding, fix requires approval)
findings.analysis: actions/* are GitHub first-party (lower risk but still non-immutable), dtolnay/rust-toolchain is third-party pinned at a mutable tag `stable`. Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies is the accepted control.
findings.remediation: Pin every uses: to a full commit SHA with the version kept as a comment (actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.x). Add a CI check or dependabot config to keep SHAs refreshed.

findings.title: Downloaded installer zip extracted and executed without SHA256 verification
evidence: no matches for SHA256|Get-FileHash|checksum|hash in install.ps1 (verified by sweep)
findings.attack: T1553.002 hash/context validation bypass on the artifact download path
findings.analysis: The release already publishes SHA256SUMS.txt (v1.0.3 asset), so verification is one fetch + one compare away; today the zip's bytes are trusted whatever arrives.
findings.remediation: After download, fetch SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release, Get-FileHash the zip, compare, fail closed with a printed mismatch; add -SkipHashCheck escape hatch for off-release local testing.

findings.title: Interactive shell functions eval remote WinUtil script (christitus.com/win) via irm|iex
findings.analysis: Vendor-recommended invocation for Chris Titus Tech WinUtil, but it is unpinned remote eval reachable from a one-word shell alias. Adjacent (unchanged) copies exist in shells/nushell/config-additions.nu:531-532 — out of recent-changes scope, flagged for awareness.
findings.remediation: Optional: front the command with a confirmation prompt, or pin a released version/hash; alternatively keep as user-choice risk acceptance (documented vendor pattern).

findings.title: Installer hardens-then-widens script execution policy (RemoteSigned, CurrentUser)
findings.analysis: RemoteSigned at CurrentUser scope is the pragmatic standard for developer machines and only permits local scripts to run unsigned, but it is a persistent policy change on the user profile without revert.
findings.remediation: Document the change in install.ps1 output (it likely is), or restore prior policy value on uninstall path (installer revoke flow).

findings.title: GITHUB_ENV write from release-asset URL-derived string
findings.analysis: Property/variable-based string, Bash-style interpolation not applicable (pwsh runner); value derives from CI-built paths, not attacker-controlled input. No command-injection sink found.
findings.remediation: None required; optionally tag with a step-scoped env file instead of the global GITHUB_ENV.

findings.title: workflow_dispatch self-input interpolated into release flow
findings.analysis: workflow_dispatch on main is a trusted event; no pull_request_target or untrusted head_ref found in either workflow.
findings.remediation: Add an input pattern validation (refs/tags/v1.*.*) to fail fast on typos.

findings.title: Subprocess spawns use fixed-string commands (no user taint in argv)
findings.evidence: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command <fixed string>; worker spawns komorebic/glazewm/pwsh/git with literal args; CI=1, telemetry optout
findings.analysis: No format!-interpolated command strings found in the spawn paths; taint limited to PATH augmentation ordering.
findings.remediation: None required; preserve the fixed-string invariant as a code-review rule.

findings.title: rustup bootstrap via curl|sh inside conformance container
findings.evidence: RUN curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal --component rustfmt --no-modify-path
findings.analysis: Vendor-standard rustup bootstrap, executed entirely inside the disposable Linux container; host isolation intact (0 host exec verified)
findings.remediation: None; optionally pin RUSTUP_INIT_VERSION in a hardening pass.

findings.title: term-launch spawns binary by CLI-name lookup (PATH/scoop ordering)
findings.evidence: format!("{}.exe", want) → command greens via Command::new(&exe).spawn(); fixed-arg spawn
findings.analysis: Trust boundary is the same user who invoked it (T1574.007 residual only, launcher semantics by design).
findings.remediation: None for a convenience launcher; keep binary lookup deterministic (scope own scoop dir first).

findings.title: Tracked binaries in repo (bin/rice-installer.exe, bin/term-launch.exe) can drift from source
findings.evidence: both files are binary entries in the 45fd6f9..HEAD diff
findings.analysis: Release artifacts (the things users run) are CI-built + SHA256SUMS.txt-hashed independently; the tracked copies are convenience/conformance artifacts. Side effect observed: their diff memory blew up the security-mcp gate (exit 134 heap OOM).
findings.remediation: Housekeeping: untrack or git-LFS the binaries, keep them in CI artifacts only.
